adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages in group.js:20-22 is off-by-one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (uses Math.floor + 1 instead of Math.ceil), making the last page unreachable and allowing clicks to 'next' that fetch an offset past the end, producing an empty member list

groups_controller.rb:23-24 accepts raw, unclamped offset and limit params with no bounds check: negative offset produces invalid SQL (OFFSET -1) causing a 500, and unbounded limit allows loading the entire membership table

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, the diff introduces `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, which are passed directly into `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no clamping/validation. This means a request with `offset=-1` will call `offset(-1)` and can generate invalid SQL for PostgreSQL (OFFSET must not be negative), causing a 500. Likewise, a very large (or negative) `limit` can effectively remove/defeat pagination (e.g., Postgres accepts `LIMIT -1` as “no limit”), allowing excessively large queries and memory usage. This is directly verifiable from the code shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members in admin/groups_controller.rb:57-63 silently succeeds when every username is unknown: unknown usernames are skipped without collecting them, the response is unconditional success_json, and admins get no feedback for a no-op add

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only calls `group.add(user)` when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user. Unknown usernames are simply skipped (no collection/reporting). Afterwards it calls `group.save` and, if it returns truthy (which it typically will even if nothing changed), it renders `success_json`. This means a request where all usernames are unknown results in a 200-success response with no indication that zero members were actually added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addMembers in admin-group.js.es6:59-62 never clears the usernames input after a successful add (only a TODO comment), so a repeat click re-sends the same names and can trigger a RecordNotUnique 500 on the server for already-member users

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `addMembers` has a `// TODO: should clear the input` and it does not clear `this.get("usernames")` after calling `model.addMembers(...)`, so the same usernames would remain in the UI. However, the finding’s stronger claim (repeat click can trigger a `RecordNotUnique` 500) is not verifiable from this diff: server-side `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` calls `group.add(user)` and `group.save`, but whether `group.add` is idempotent or can raise on duplicates depends on Group model code not shown here. So the concrete issue is at most a UX/missing-polish item, not a clearly provable correctness/500 error from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin-group-selector.hbs is reduced to a bare <input type="text"> with no value binding, silently dropping the component's selection contract so consumers reading the selected group(s) now get nothing

adjudication.rationale: The diff for `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/components/admin-group-selector.hbs` only removes blank lines; the template content remains exactly `<input type="text">` both before and after. No value binding or selection-related behavior was removed in this change, so the finding misreads the diff and is not a verifiable new defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test coverage for the new public members JSON envelope: findMembers depends on result.meta.total, result.meta.limit, result.meta.offset, and result.members, but groups_controller.rb#members has zero specs covering the meta contract, total count, or pagination correctness

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to return a new JSON envelope `{ members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }` and updates `Discourse.Group#findMembers` to depend on `result.meta.total`, `result.meta.limit`, `result.meta.offset`, and `result.members`. However, the only spec file touched is `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`, and there are no added/updated specs for `GroupsController#members` (or any coverage asserting the new `meta` contract, total count correctness, or pagination behavior). So the statement that this new public response format has zero spec coverage in the diff is verifiably true.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public group members page (group/members.hbs) has no pagination UI despite server limiting members to 50 with meta paging, so groups with >50 members silently show only the first 50 to regular users — a user-visible capability regression

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply `limit`/`offset` for *all* groups, defaulting to `limit = 50` (previously only automatic groups were limited, and non-automatic groups returned the full list). On the client, `Discourse.Group#findMembers` now requests `members.json` with `limit`/`offset` and stores results in `members` plus `meta` (`user_count`, `limit`, `offset`). However, the public group members UI (`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs`) only changes from iterating `model` to iterating `members` and adds no pagination controls, and `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` just calls `model.findMembers()` with the default offset 0. Therefore, for groups with >50 members, regular users will only see the first 50 with no pagination UI in this diff, which is a user-visible regression introduced by these changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages in admin-group.js.es6 uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, producing a phantom empty page for exact multiples (e.g. 50/50 yields 2 pages); should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit)
removeMember never re-clamps offset against the new user_count after membership mutation, so removing the last member on the final page leaves the admin on an empty page with no auto-correction

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. `removeMember` calls `self.findMembers()` after deletion without adjusting `offset`. In `findMembers`, the requested `offset` is clamped using the *current* `this.get("user_count")` (which is stale until the AJAX returns):

```js
var offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0));
...
Discourse.ajax(..., { data: { limit: ..., offset: offset } })
```

If you are on the last page (e.g. `limit=50`, `user_count=51`, `offset=50`) and remove the only member on that page, the new total becomes 50 but the reload still requests `offset=50`. `GroupsController#members` then does `limit(limit).offset(offset)` with `total=50, offset=50`, producing an empty `members` array and returning `meta.offset=50`, and the client persists `offset=50` with `user_count=50`—leaving the admin view stuck on an empty page with no auto-correction.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin-group-selector.hbs contains a bare, unbound <input type="text"> with no value binding, placeholder, or action — dead scaffolding unrelated to the diff that renders a dead text input for any consumer

adjudication.rationale: The diff in admin-group-selector.hbs only removes surrounding blank lines; the template content remains a single `<input type="text">` both before and after. So the change does not introduce a new “dead input” defect. Also, from the diff alone it’s not verifiable that this input is unbound/unused, because Ember components often attach behavior via the component JS (not shown here) rather than Handlebars `value=` bindings or explicit actions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members in admin/groups_controller.rb silently swallows unknown usernames with no else branch, returning success_json for partial additions like 'alice,bogus_name' with zero feedback to the admin

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only calls `group.add(user)` inside `if user = User.find_by_username(username)`. There is no `else` handling for unknown usernames, and the action renders `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds (which it likely will even if no users were found/added). Therefore a request like `alice,bogus_name` will add only existing users and still return success with no feedback about invalid usernames.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Whitespace-only reformatting of user-selector-autocomplete.raw.hbs (plus equivalent churn: ilike → ILIKE with no semantic change, controller/find_group re-indentation) creates review noise and merge conflicts unrelated to group membership

adjudication.rationale: The cited changes are purely formatting/casing refactors in the diff: `user-selector-autocomplete.raw.hbs` only changes indentation/newlines, `ilike` → `ILIKE` is SQL keyword casing with no behavioral change, and `find_group` is just re-indented. While this may be “review noise,” it is not a bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the patch; claims about merge conflicts are speculative.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CSS restructuring in admin_base.scss re-scopes form styling as .groups, .badges, coupling the badges admin UI to this PR's group UI rework so future group form adjustments silently restyle badges forms

adjudication.rationale: The diff does move shared `.form-horizontal` styling from `section.details` into a new scoped block `.groups, .badges { .form-horizontal { ... } }`, which indeed means badges pages will use the same form styling as groups. However, the proposed finding claims this is a *problem* because future group-form tweaks would “silently” restyle badges. That is speculative and not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff itself. From the diff alone we can’t establish that badges should not share these styles, nor that this causes an actual bug/correctness issue now.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The GET /admin/groups/users route is deleted with no replacement or deprecation shim, breaking any plugin, script, or API consumer that uses the endpoint with no migration path

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `get "users"` member route under `admin/groups` in `config/routes.rb`, but the proposed finding is not precise and overstates the issue. The removed route would have been `/admin/groups/:group_id/users` (not `/admin/groups/users`). Also, the codebase clearly migrates group membership listing to `GET /groups/:group_id/members.json` (`Discourse.Group#findMembers`) and adds new admin endpoints for membership changes (`PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members.json`). Whether any external plugin/script/API consumer is broken is speculative and not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id) bypassing Group#remove, skipping destroy callbacks and side effects, making add and remove paths semantically inconsistent

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` does use `group.users.delete(user_id)` while `#add_members` uses `group.add(user)`, so the paths are inconsistent. However, the proposed finding’s core claim—that this “bypasses `Group#remove`, skipping destroy callbacks and side effects” and therefore introduces a real defect—is not verifiable from the diff because the implementation/semantics of `Group#remove` (and any callbacks/side effects it might perform) are not shown. It’s plausible in Rails that `association.delete` skips callbacks on join records, but asserting a concrete bug here depends on code not present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member commits the association delete before group.save, so error handling on save failure reports failure for an already-committed mutation that cannot be rolled back, leaving user_count stale

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then checks `if group.save ... else ...`. While the association delete is executed immediately (not wrapped in a transaction here), the diff does not show any change to `group` attributes that could cause `group.save` to fail, and for a persisted, valid group a subsequent `save` is very likely to succeed (or be a no-op). The proposed claim about leaving `user_count` stale is also not supported by the diff: `remove_member` renders only `success_json`/errors (no `user_count`), and the JS model’s `removeMember` reloads members via `findMembers()`, which recomputes `meta.total` from `group.users.count`. So the finding depends on speculative validation failures not evidenced in the diff and misstates the `user_count` behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Breaking unversioned change to PUT /admin/groups/:id and POST /admin/groups contract: params switched from nested (params[:group][:alias_level], etc.) to flat, PATCH verb removed

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Admin::GroupsController API payload shape and supported semantics. Previously, create/update expected nested params under `params[:group]` (e.g., `params[:group][:name]`, `params[:group][:alias_level]`, `params[:group][:visible]`, and usernames/membership changes), and `update` explicitly handled PATCH via `update_patch` for incremental membership changes. In the new code, `create` reads flat params (`params[:name]`, `params[:visible]`), `update` reads flat params (`params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`, `params[:name]`) and no longer has `update_patch`/PATCH-specific behavior, while membership changes are moved to separate `/admin/groups/:group_id/members` PUT/DELETE endpoints. This is a verifiable breaking change for any client still sending the old nested `group` payload or relying on PATCH incremental updates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unversioned contract change causes params[:visible] to be nil for old clients, silently setting group visible to false, while alias_level/name changes are silently ignored with a 200 response

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff changes the Admin::GroupsController API contract from nested params[:group][...] (old code in create/update_put) to top-level params[:name], params[:alias_level], params[:visible] (new create/update). Old clients still sending { group: { visible: ..., name: ..., alias_level: ... } } will now have params[:visible] == nil, so `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` will set visible to false, and params[:name]/:alias_level will be nil so those updates will be skipped/ignored. The controller will still return success (200) as long as group.save succeeds, making the break silent. This is directly verifiable from the before/after controller code in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently drops unknown usernames and returns success_json regardless, so admins get no feedback that zero members were added

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only adds users that exist (`if user = User.find_by_username(username) ... end`), silently ignoring unknown usernames. After the loop it renders `success_json` whenever `group.save` succeeds. Since `group.save` will typically succeed even if no users were found/added (no validation failure), the endpoint can return success even when zero members were added, giving admins no feedback about dropped/unknown usernames.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members performs N+1 queries with find_by_username inside a loop instead of a single WHERE username_lower IN (...) query, and is non-atomic so mid-loop failure leaves a partially-added group

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the diff shows `usernames.split(",").each` and inside the loop it calls `User.find_by_username(username)` for each entry, which will issue one query per username (an N-query pattern) instead of a single `WHERE ... IN (...)` lookup. The loop also calls `group.add(user)` repeatedly without wrapping the operation in a transaction; since adding to an ActiveRecord association typically persists each join row immediately, an exception or later failure (e.g., `group.save` failing) could leave some users already added and others not, making the operation non-atomic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members never strips whitespace from usernames, so input like " bob" silently matches no user

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code takes `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and iterates `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` without trimming whitespace. It then calls `User.find_by_username(username)`, which will not match if `username` has leading/trailing spaces (e.g., " bob"). This means such input will silently result in no user being added, matching the proposed finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages calculation uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, producing a phantom empty page for exact multiples (e.g., 100/50 yields 3 pages instead of 2); should use Math.ceil
Pagination limit parameter in groups_controller#members is unbounded, allowing limit=1000000 to serialize the entire member list in one public request

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then uses it directly in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no upper bound or clamp. A client who can access the group members endpoint (subject only to `guardian.ensure_can_see!(group)`) can pass an arbitrarily large `limit` (e.g., 1000000), causing the server to load and serialize a very large number of users in one request, which is a verifiable performance/DoS risk introduced/left unmitigated by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Group members fetch failure path degrades from route abort to silently empty list: setupController fire-and-forgets findMembers with no rejection handling, making 'failed to load' indistinguishable from 'no members'
findMembers return-value meaning changed: returns undefined when name is empty instead of a resolved promise of []
matched_golden_ids: Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that `findMembers` can return `undefined` on a certain code path (when `name` is empty), which is the same underlying issue as the golden comment: not all function paths explicitly return a value, leading to `undefined`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pagination state (limit, offset, members, user_count) stored as mutable properties on the shared Discourse.Group model causes stale state across admin editor, group-members page, and findPosts flows

next/previous writes offset before the fetch resolves, so rapid clicks fire concurrent findMembers calls that can resolve out of order, leaving members and meta.offset permanently inconsistent with the actual page
matched_golden_ids: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same underlying problem: findMembers() is asynchronous and not properly handled/awaited, which can create race conditions. The candidate elaborates a specific manifestation (rapid clicks causing concurrent calls that resolve out of order and desync offset vs members), which is consistent with the golden concern about member data not being available immediately.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Parallel service paths for membership mutation (group.add, group.users.delete, orphaned Group#remove) mean side-effect invariants are enforced on only one path and will drift when side effects are added

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces two different code paths for changing group membership: `add_members` uses `group.add(user)` while `remove_member` uses `group.users.delete(user_id)`. These are not symmetric operations and, in Rails, `association.delete` typically bypasses model-level logic/callbacks that a domain method like `group.remove(user)` (used in the previous implementation) would encapsulate. This makes it plausible and reviewable that any side effects/invariants (e.g., counter caches like `user_count`, auditing, denormalized fields, callbacks on the join model) will be enforced on the add path but skipped on the remove path, leading to drift. The finding’s mention of an “orphaned Group#remove” is not directly verifiable from the diff (the method isn’t shown), but the core issue—parallel mutation paths with potentially different side effects—is real in the changed controller code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member returns success (200) when removing a non-member since users.delete of an absent id is a no-op, giving API consumers indistinguishable success for real and zero-op changes

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#remove_member, the code does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then returns `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds. If the user_id is not currently a member, `delete` on an AR association is typically a no-op and will not raise, so the endpoint will still return success. However, this is consistent with common idempotent DELETE semantics (repeating a delete can still return 200/204), and the diff does not establish a requirement that removing a non-member must error or be distinguishable. So this is more of an API design preference than a verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PATCH membership API silently deleted in GroupsController#update; PATCH requests with changes payload now no-op and return HTTP 200, causing silent data-integrity drift for external API consumers

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the PATCH-specific membership update logic in `Admin::GroupsController#update`. Previously, `update` branched on `request.patch?` to `update_patch(group)`, which processed `params[:changes][:add]`/`[:delete]` to add/remove users. Now `update` always applies only `alias_level`, `visible`, and (if not automatic) `name`, and never reads `params[:changes]`. Since Rails routes PATCH to `update`, a PATCH request with a `changes` payload will be ignored; `group.save` will typically succeed even with no changes, returning `success_json` (HTTP 200), making the membership update a silent no-op. New `add_members`/`remove_member` endpoints are added, but the old PATCH behavior is indeed deleted without an error response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Full-set membership sync via group:usernames payload silently dropped from GroupsController#update; clients sending the old documented PUT shape get success_json with no membership change

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::GroupsController#update` no longer reads `params[:group]` (the old PUT payload shape) and specifically no longer processes `payload[:usernames]` to sync membership. Instead it only updates `alias_level`, `visible`, and (if not automatic) `name`, and then returns `success_json` on save. Therefore, a client still sending the previous documented shape like `PUT /admin/groups/:id { group: { usernames: "a,b" } }` will get a successful response while the membership change is ignored (membership updates have been moved to the new `add_members`/`remove_member` endpoints).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Create-group-with-initial-members objective dropped: GroupsController#create no longer consumes params[:group][:usernames], and the group.hbs template wraps member UI in {{#if id}} so new groups cannot be given members at creation time

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes support for supplying initial members when creating a group. On the client, `group.createWithUsernames(this.get('usernames'))` was replaced with `group.create()`, and `Discourse.Group#asJSON` no longer includes `usernames`. On the server, `Admin::GroupsController#create` now reads `params[:name]`/`params[:visible]` and no longer consumes `params[:group][:usernames]` (or any usernames param) to add members during creation. Additionally, the admin template wraps the members/add-members UI in `{{#if id}}`, so before the group is saved (no id) there is no UI path to add members at creation time. This is a concrete functional regression compared to the prior behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public GET /groups/:name/members JSON contract changed from a bare serialized array to {members: [...], meta: {...}} without acceptance, silently breaking consumers of the old array shape

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (which returns a bare JSON array of serialized users) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }`, i.e. an object with `members` and `meta` keys. The client code was updated accordingly (`group.findMembers()` now expects `result.meta` and `result.members`). Any other consumer of `GET /groups/:group_id/members(.json)` expecting the previous array shape would break, so the finding is a real, verifiable contract change introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public group page silently truncates to 50 members: findMembers() sends limit 50, the server now applies the limit to all groups (previously only automatic groups), and group/members.hbs has no pagination controls

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Discourse.Group.findMembers()` the client now always requests `/groups/:name/members.json` with `limit`/`offset`, defaulting to `limit: 50` (`limit: 50, offset: 0` added to the model). On the server, `GroupsController#members` was changed to apply `limit`/`offset` for all groups (previously it only paginated automatic groups; non-automatic groups returned the full list). The public group members route (`discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`) now just calls `model.findMembers()` and the template (`discourse/templates/group/members.hbs`) iterates `{{#each m in members}}` but adds no pagination controls/actions, so only the first 50 members will be displayed with no way to navigate further, i.e. silent truncation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AdminGroupController totalPages off-by-one: Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 yields a phantom empty page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit; needs a ceiling calculation instead

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` (when `user_count != 0`). If `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 50/50 or 100/50), this returns one extra page (2 or 3 respectively) even though only 1 or 2 pages have members. This also affects navigation: `showingLast` compares `currentPage` to this inflated `totalPages`, so on the real last page it will incorrectly allow `next`, and `next` sets `offset` to `user_count`, leading `findMembers()` to request an empty page (offset beyond the last record). A ceiling-based calculation (e.g., `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`) would avoid the phantom empty page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member raw-deletes the join row via group.users.delete(user_id), bypassing GroupUser callbacks and dropping the user_count maintenance the old group.remove(user) path performed, leaving stale member counts

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, member removal in `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` is implemented as `group.users.delete(user_id)` followed by `group.save`. Previously, removals went through `group.remove(user)` (see the deleted `update_patch` path), while additions still use `group.add(user)` in the new `add_members` action. This asymmetry is a concrete change: the new code bypasses whatever logic `Group#remove` encapsulated (e.g., updating cached `user_count`, related bookkeeping, or any join-model behavior), and `group.save` alone does not guarantee membership-derived counters are recomputed. Thus the finding points to a real risk introduced by the diff: removing via the association directly can leave derived state like `user_count` stale compared to the prior `group.remove` path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Spec 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' uses xhr :put instead of delete, so PUT is routed to add_members and the 422 assertion passes for the wrong reason without testing remove_member's automatic-group guard
Status-code contract for automatic-group modification changed from 403 (Discourse::InvalidAccess) to 422 (can_not_modify_automatic) without acceptance, breaking clients that branch on 403

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the old PATCH-based membership modification path that raised `Discourse::InvalidAccess` for automatic groups (`update_patch`), which the spec previously asserted returned HTTP 403 (see removed test `cannot patch automatic groups ... response.status.should == 403`). Membership modification is now handled by new endpoints `add_members`/`remove_member`, and both explicitly `return can_not_modify_automatic if group.automatic`, where `can_not_modify_automatic` renders status 422. The updated spec also expects 422 for automatic-group member adds. So the status code for this class of automatic-group modification has verifiably changed from 403 to 422 in the diff, which can break clients that branch on 403.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently swallows nonexistent usernames: typos are skipped with no error and the endpoint responds 200 with success_json, giving admins no signal that some members were not added

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only adds a user when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a record. If a username is misspelled/nonexistent, it is simply skipped (no error collected or returned). The action then renders `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, which it likely will even when some/most usernames were ignored. Therefore an admin can get a 200 success response without being told that some requested members were not added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: groups_controller.rb:24 limit param has no upper bound, allowing a single request with ?limit=100000000 to materialize and serialize entire group membership, enabling resource exhaustion and full member-list scraping

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff introduces `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then directly applies it to the query: `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` and serializes the resulting `members`. There is no clamp/maximum enforced on `limit`, so a request like `?limit=100000000` can cause the server to load and serialize an extremely large number of users, creating a plausible resource-exhaustion vector and enabling bulk member-list extraction in one request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New meta.limit is echoed back unvalidated, and the client (group.js findMembers) trusts and adopts it as its page size
groups_controller.rb:23-24 offset and limit have no lower-bound clamp; negative values like limit=-1 or offset=-1 reach PostgreSQL causing unhandled 500 errors on a public endpoint

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then directly applies them via `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no lower-bound checks. If a client supplies a negative offset (e.g., `offset=-1`), ActiveRecord will generate SQL with a negative OFFSET, which PostgreSQL rejects ("OFFSET must not be negative"), resulting in an unhandled 500 on this endpoint. This is a concrete, verifiable correctness issue introduced/expanded by the change (pagination now applies to all groups, not just automatic ones).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `totalPages` in admin-group.js.es6 is off-by-one for user counts that are exact multiples of limit (Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1), yielding a phantom empty page (e.g. 100 users / 50 limit shows 3 pages instead of 2) with 'next' enabled on the last real page
matched_golden_ids: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same pagination edge case: when user_count is an exact multiple of the page limit, the logic allows/creates an extra "next"/page that yields an empty results page (phantom last page), causing confusing UX on the final page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New pagination behavior in admin-group.js.es6 (currentPage/totalPages/next/previous actions, clamping in findMembers, empty-page state, user_count == 0 early returns) ships with zero test assertions

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce new pagination-related logic in the Ember admin group controller/model (currentPage/totalPages, next/previous, limit/offset handling, updated members API response). However, the proposed finding is about the absence of tests for that new client-side pagination behavior. While it’s true the diff adds no JS/Ember tests asserting pagination behavior, “no tests” is not itself a concrete bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the diff; it’s a process/coverage concern. The diff does add/modify Ruby controller specs, but they are unrelated to asserting the new pagination UI logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: groups_controller_spec .update test only covers the !group.automatic guard's false side; the non-automatic rename branch's changed contract (usernames removed from payload, name/alias_level now read from top-level params) has no test, so a regression breaking all group renames would keep the suite green

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes Admin::GroupsController#update to read `name`, `alias_level`, and `visible` from top-level params (e.g., `params[:name]`) instead of from `params[:group]` (old `payload = params[:group]`). In the updated `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`, the only remaining `.update` test is `"ignore name change on automatic group"`, which exercises only the automatic-group guard (`group.name = params[:name] if ... && !group.automatic`). There is no test covering the non-automatic branch to ensure a regular group can still be renamed / updated with the new parameter contract. Thus a regression that breaks renames/updates for non-automatic groups could indeed leave the suite green.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The replacement .update spec only asserts the automatic-group ignore case (group.name.should_not == "WAT"), which can pass vacuously, and the old spec asserting group.name == 'fred' was deleted

adjudication.rationale: The diff does replace the previous non-automatic update/member-management specs with a single `.update` example that only covers the automatic-group rename-ignore behavior. However, the new assertion is not purely vacuous: it also checks `group.visible.should == true` after `xhr :put, :update`, which would fail if the update action didn’t execute or didn’t persist changes. The removal of the old `group.name.should == 'fred'` test reduces coverage for renaming non-automatic groups, but that is a test-suite coverage change rather than a verifiable functional defect introduced by the code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The remove_member spec invokes the action with the wrong verb (xhr :put, :remove_member instead of delete), testing an invocation path that never exists in the running app
matched_golden_ids: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that the remove_member spec/test uses xhr :put to hit remove_member, but the actual route/action expects a DELETE request, so the test is exercising a non-existent invocation path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: None of the new specs exercise the routes added in config/routes.rb (delete "members" => "groups#remove_member", put "members" => "groups#add_members", removal of get "users"), so route typos or param-name mismatches would break the admin UI while tests stay green

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add new member routes under `admin/groups` and the updated specs invoke controller actions directly (`xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: ...`) rather than making a request through the router, so they don’t validate the routing table itself. However, this is not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff: the route-to-action mapping and parameter name (`:group_id`) match what the controller and JS client code use (`/admin/groups/:id/members.json` -> `group_id`), so there’s no demonstrated route typo or mismatch in the diff—only a hypothetical gap in test coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently skips unknown usernames (User.find_by_username with no else branch), returning success_json with no feedback while group.users.count is unchanged, and the new spec suite dropped the old explicit test for this documented behavior

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the loop does `if user = User.find_by_username(username); group.add(user); end` and provides no error/feedback for unknown usernames; if all usernames are unknown, `group.save` will still succeed and it will render `success_json`. However, the removed code path (the old PATCH `update_patch`) behaved the same way and even had an explicit spec asserting “succeeds silently when adding non-existent users”, indicating this is intentional behavior rather than a defect introduced by this diff. Dropping that spec is a test-coverage change, not a verifiable runtime bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members' naive usernames.split(",") fails on inputs with spaces like "bob, alice", silently skipping every member after the first

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code does `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` and then looks up `User.find_by_username(username)`. If the input is "bob, alice", the second token will be " alice" (leading space), causing `find_by_username` to fail and that user to be skipped. There is no `strip`/whitespace normalization per token, so the behavior is exactly as described and would silently skip any usernames with leading/trailing spaces.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member succeeds unconditionally (200) for a non-member or already-deleted user_id since group.users.delete is a no-op and group.save returns true on an unchanged model, and no test covers removing a user who isn't in the group (the old 'succeeds silently when removing non-members' test was dropped)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `remove_member` does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then returns `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds, which will likely be true even when `user_id` is not currently a member. However, the previous implementation explicitly had a test asserting this behavior (“succeeds silently when removing non-members”), indicating that returning success on a no-op removal was acceptable/intentional (idempotent delete). The fact that the specific test was removed is a coverage change, not a verifiable correctness bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In admin/groups_controller.rb remove_member, group.users.delete(user_id) bypasses the sanctioned group.remove(user) path and skips callbacks that maintain the denormalized groups.user_count column, and the trailing group.save is a no-op, leaving user_count silently out of sync with actual group_users rows (silent data corruption) until a manual refresh_automatic_groups or re-add

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `remove_member` now does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then calls `group.save`. It’s true this bypasses the previously-used `group.remove(user)` API (seen in the removed incremental update code), and `group.save` likely won’t affect the join deletion. However, the finding’s core claim—silent corruption of a denormalized `groups.user_count` because callbacks/counter maintenance are skipped—is not verifiable from the diff: we can’t see how `user_count` is maintained (counter_cache vs. custom `Group#add/#remove` logic), nor whether `group.users.delete` triggers the relevant callbacks/counter updates in this app. The assertion about needing `refresh_automatic_groups` also doesn’t follow from the shown logic (it’s unrelated to non-automatic group membership counts).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The old membership-write contract (group[usernames] and changes[add]/[delete] params) is removed in the same commit that rewrites the client with no expand/contract window: cached old admin JS sends group: {...} which the new update silently ignores and returns success (silent membership no-op), while new JS sends flat name/visible/alias_level to an old update_put where params[:group] is nil, causing a NoMethodError 500; API scripts using the removed incremental membership PATCH get a silent 200 that does nothing

In admin/groups_controller.rb add_members, membership additions are not atomic and failures are swallowed: nonexistent usernames are skipped without error while success_json is returned, and a duplicate-membership unique index violation makes group.save fail after in-memory association mutation, returning a generic 422 with no indication which usernames were dropped

adjudication.rationale: The new `add_members` action does silently skip usernames that don’t resolve (`User.find_by_username` returning nil) and can still return `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds, so “nonexistent usernames are skipped without error” is grounded in the diff. However, the rest of the finding (duplicate-membership unique-index violation during `group.save` after only in-memory mutation, non-atomicity specifics, and the exact failure mode) depends on the implementation of `Group#add` / association behavior and database constraints, none of which are shown in the diff. Since the claimed unique-index violation and `group.save` failure scenario aren’t verifiable from the provided changes and prior tests indicate silent skipping was previously accepted behavior, the finding as stated is not a strictly verifiable defect in this diff.
